description:
Find listed replacement opcodes not explained by direct constructors in an entry.

This is advisory. Helpers, retained operations, mutation, and constructors outside
an entry's span can explain a candidate. APInt/ConstantExpr computations do not
by themselves create runtime instructions. Never remove an opcode automatically.

Convert add/or/sub combining logical high-bit extraction with a conditional sign-extension magic pattern into arithmetic shift (and restore truncation if needed).
For two pointer expressions sharing a base, compute GEP byte offsets, subtract them, and cast the result to integer; may rewrite GEP offsets and add NUW based on inbounds/no-wrap metadata.
~X - min/max(~X,Y) -> ~min/max(X,~Y) - X, when Y is cheaply invertible and the complemented operand has fewer than three uses.
min/max(~X,Y) - ~X -> X - ~min/max(X,~Y), when Y is cheaply invertible and the complemented operand has fewer than three uses.
Subtract zero-extended ptrtoint/ptrtoaddr operands where LHS is a nowrap GEP of RHS pointer -> zext/sext GEP byte offset.
Combine equality-of-low/high adjacent extracted integer parts into one comparison of the wider extracted parts.
Substitute a known constant into the other comparison under logical AND/OR with a constant equality guard.
and(zext(A),B) -> select(A,B&1,0).

candidates.description: (A&B)|(C&D) -> bitcast(select(Cond, bitcast(B), bitcast(D))), where getSelectCondition recognizes complementary masks A/C and derives the scalar/vector i1 Cond. For (A&B)|~(A|D), derive Cond from the identical masks and complement D before selecting.
Fold (X==C)|(Y<X-C) or dual form into one adjusted unsigned comparison.

For input `xor(icmp,icmp)` in the paired-comparison truth-table case, when the comparison selected for inversion has one use, invert its predicate and produce `and(LHS,RHS)` from the simplified OR/AND pair.
For input `xor(icmp,icmp)` in the paired-comparison truth-table case with shared uses of Y, invert Y, insert NOT after it, replace its other uses, enqueue users, then produce `and(LHS,RHS)`.
not(bitcast(compare)) -> bitcast(inverse-predicate compare).
Replace aligned power-of-two transfer of 1/2/4/8 bytes with integer load/store, preserving metadata, volatility, atomic-unordered ordering, and then zero transfer length.

Lower constant-length memset of 1/2/4/8 bytes to store: replicate constant byte across bytes or accept nonconstant byte only for length 1; preserve alignment, volatile, atomic unordered, debug/alias metadata; zero original length.
All-ones masked gather from splat pointer becomes scalar load plus vector splat.
For recognized power-of-two input, cttz -> log2(input); ctlz -> bitwidth-1-log2(input), setting NSW and NUW on the latter subtraction.

For ARM NEON signed/unsigned shift intrinsics with constant, uniform, in-range shift amounts, lower nonnegative amounts to shl; lower negative amounts to ashr for signed variants or lshr for unsigned variants, using the negated amount.
Replace umax(nuw_shl(x,C), x+1) with select(x==0,1,nuw_shl(x,C)) for nonzero C; or use nuw_mul(x,C) only when C is neither zero nor one. Both commutative operand orders are tried.
For approximate powi(2.0,p), replace with ldexp(1.0,p), splatting exponent to vector width when needed.
Combine ptrmask(ptrmask(p,A),B) into ptrmask(p,A & B) by replacing the pointer and mask operands.
Move a single-use fneg from a larger matrix operand to the smaller other operand when element-count profitability conditions hold.
Remove nonnull bundle if known nonzero; otherwise transfer it to load metadata or an inbounds GEP base assumption.
Within bounded safe-to-speculate window, remove adjacent duplicate guard or merge guard(a); guard(b) into guard(a&b), moving intervening instructions before first guard.

For a defined callee with incompatible calling convention, insert the poison-pointer store marker and replace a nonvoid result with poison. Erase an ordinary call; preserve invoke/callbr CFG edges and replace their callee with null.

For an undefined null or undef callee, replace a nonvoid result with poison. Preserve invoke/callbr unchanged as terminators; for an ordinary call, insert the poison-pointer store marker and erase the call.
Replace truncation of an OR of opposite shifts with a narrower llvm.fshl or llvm.fshr call, narrowing operands and shift amount.
Move a truncation through a logical or arithmetic right shift of a truncated operand when the shift amount is small enough that discarded shifted-in bits cannot affect the result.
Evaluate the source expression in an intermediate integer type twice the destination width, then truncate once to the requested destination width.
Replace trunc(lshr(sext(a), C)) with sext/trunc(ashr(a, narrowed C)) when the source type differs from the trunc destination.
Replace zext(x slt 0) with logical shift right by the source sign-bit position, then zero-extend/truncate that 0/1 result to the zext type.

When KnownBits proves the compared value has exactly one possible set bit, replace zext(eq/ne x,0) with the corresponding shifted low bit, toggling it for equality and casting to the zext type if needed.
Replace zext(eq/ne (and x, 1<<shift), 0) with the selected shifted bit, complemented for equality, masked to one bit and cast to the extension result type.
After evaluating the zext source expression in the destination type, clear any high bits that may differ with an AND mask.
Replace sext(x slt 0) with arithmetic shift right by the source sign-bit position, then sign-extend/truncate to the sext type.

For a one-bit KnownBits source and equality test against zero or its sole possible set bit, replace sext of the comparison with either (x >> n)-1 or ((x << n) ashr signbit), preserving the comparison polarity.
Replace sext(trunc(lshr(y,C))) with sext/trunc(ashr(y,C)) when C is within the discarded-bit range and the sign-bit analysis proves the logical shift filled bits agree with the destination sign.
When the widened source expression lacks enough sign bits, implement sign extension as shl then arithmetic shift right by the width difference.
Replace sext(ashr(trunc(x), source_width-1)) with shl/ashr sign-bit propagation on x, then sign-cast to destination when needed.
Replace fptoui/fptosi(fdiv(uitofp/sitofp(x), exact integer-valued C)) with udiv/sdiv(x,C).
Normalize inttoptr input width to the target intptr width with zext or trunc before inttoptr.
Normalize ptrtoint to target intptr width followed by zext/trunc to the requested integer width.
Replace a closed web of opposite bitcasts and PHIs with PHIs in the source type, combining eligible simple loads and redirecting stores and cast users to the new PHIs.
Replace the load comparison with `(Idx == FirstTrueIdx) | (Idx == SecondTrueIdx)` when exactly two indexed elements satisfy the predicate.

Rewrite (x | y) eq/ne y as (~x | y) eq/ne all-ones when x can be freely inverted.

Apply the same reversible arithmetic offset to both operands of an integer equality/inequality, recursively transforming one-use select arms when the offset operation simplifies and preserves poison.
Canonicalize equality/inequality of x with one-use rotate-right(x) to equality/inequality of x with rotate-left(x).
For equality/inequality between zext and sext of i1 operands, compare their bitwise or against zero.

candidates.description: For unsigned less-than against a constant outside the representable signed-extension range, check whether source operand is nonnegative.
For unsigned greater-than against a constant outside the representable signed-extension range, check whether source operand is negative.
Replace zero-extended add and overflow comparison by a width-normalized add plus unsigned wrap comparison against an operand.
Move a comparison before a one-use shuffle with splat/poison mask and splat constant.
Move comparison through a shuffle with splat/poison mask and splat constant, rebuilding a shuffle after elementwise compare.
Peel a nuw left shift from an unsigned comparison by evaluating the other operand shifted right logically.
Peel an nsw left shift from a non-unsigned comparison by evaluating the other operand shifted right arithmetically.
Invert both operands and swap comparison predicate when this removes an inversion operation.
For a simple one-field struct load, issue one load of its field type and rebuild the struct with insertvalue from poison.
For a simple one-element array load, load its element type and rebuild the array with insertvalue from poison.
Rewrite load(protected_field_ptr(...)) as ptrauth.auth of a cloned load from the underlying pointer, with pointer/integer casts and preserved deactivation bundle.
For a simple one-field struct store, extract its field, build a store of the field type at the same pointer, and erase the aggregate store.
For a simple one-element array store, extract the element and build a store of the element type at the same pointer.
Rewrite store(value, protected_field_ptr(ptr)) to store(ptrauth.sign(value), ptr), preserving optional deactivation-symbol bundle.
(lshr X,bitwidth-1)*Y -> select(X<0,Y,0), including commuted operands.
Under reassoc+nnan, powi(X,Y)/(X*Z) -> powi(X,Y-1)/Z if exponent subtraction cannot signed-overflow.
(X/C1)*C -> X*(C/C1) when the folded quotient is normal; if that quotient is denormal, use X/(C1/C) when the inner division is one-use and alternate quotient is normal.
(X+C1)*C -> (X*C)+(C*C1) when constant product folds.
(C1-X)*C -> (C*C1)-(X*C) when constant product folds.
For signed division by select(cond,1,Y), replace with select(cond,X,sdiv(X,Y)); source permits this only when Y is a nonzero constant other than -1.
For unsigned division by select(cond,1,Y), replace with select(cond,X,udiv(X,Y)); source requires the non-unit divisor to be known nonzero and nonpoison.
For signed division by select(cond,Y,1), replace with select(cond,sdiv(X,Y),X); source permits this only when Y is a nonzero constant other than -1.
For unsigned division by select(cond,Y,1), replace with select(cond,udiv(X,Y),X); source requires the non-unit divisor to be known nonzero and nonpoison.
log2(zext X) -> zext(log2(X)), recursively extracting the logarithm.
log2(trunc X) -> trunc(log2(X)) when nonzero is assumed or trunc is NUW.
log2(select(C,X,Y)) -> select(C,log2(X),log2(Y)) when both arms recursively simplify.
x udiv negative-known y -> zext(x>=u y).
x udiv sext(i1 b) -> zext(x == -1).
Cross-instruction transformation of 1/sqrt(a), x*x and a/sqrt(a) into 1/a, sqrt(a), and products, replacing/removing matched instructions.
Under reassoc and available tan libfunc, sin(X)/cos(X)->tan(X), cos(X)/sin(X)->1/tan(X).
1 urem x -> zext(x != 1).
For true negation of (lshr(X,C) & 1), construct the sign mask by shl(X,(W-1)-C), then ashr by W-1, and truncate/bitcast to the original and type.
Replace one-use integer-PHI-to-inttoptr with a new pointer PHI, inserting per-edge bit/pointer casts for incoming values that need conversion; erase original inttoptr and integer PHI.

Replace a PHI with at least three incoming values, at least two one-use zexts from one narrow type and at least one losslessly truncatable constant, by a narrow PHI followed by zext/bitcast to original type.
Replace a zero-versus-power-of-two select controlled by an AND-mask equality with a masked shift/cast expression, optionally XORing the selected power-of-two constant.
Factor a common base/index operand from two identical one-use two-operand GEPs, select the differing operand, and rebuild one GEP with intersected no-wrap flags.
Flip a canonical relational comparison threshold when its adjusted constant matches a select arm, then swap the select arms and profile metadata.
Canonicalize icmp sgt X, -1 select to an isneg(X) condition and swap the select arms.
For select(C,shuffle(X,Y),X), select Y versus X first and shuffle X with that result.

candidates.description: Rewrite select(C&B,A,B) as select(B,select(~C,true,A),false).
Rewrite select(A|C,A,B) as select(A,true,select(~C,B,false)).
Flatten select(C0, select(C1,a,b), b) into select(C0 && C1,a,b) for the direct C1 true-arm match; the combined condition uses short-circuit logical AND.
Flatten select(C0, select(C1,b,a), b) into select(C0 && !C1,a,b) when inner true arm equals outer false arm; the combined condition uses short-circuit logical AND.
Flatten select(C0,a,select(C1,a,b)) into select(C0 || C1,a,b) for the direct inner true-arm match; the combined condition uses short-circuit logical OR.
Flatten select(C0,a,select(C1,b,a)) into select(C0 || !C1,a,b) when inner false arm equals outer true arm; the combined condition uses short-circuit logical OR.
Replace shift amount A srem 2^k with A & (2^k-1), then use that as the shift amount.
Narrow bswap(zext X) before lshr when shift amount is at least the width difference: zext(bswap(X) lshr (C-widthdiff)).
Narrow bswap(zext X) before lshr when shift amount is below width difference: shl(zext(bswap(X)), widthdiff-C).
Propagate shifted demanded bits to source, demanding sign bit when shifted-in bits are observed; drop exact flag if operand changes.
Replace ctpop(not X) when only parity is demanded and source width is even with ctpop(X).
Fold masked low GEP offset bits into the constant GEP index when pointer alignment proves those low bits zero before ptrmask.
Rewrite fdiv(x,x) as select of qNaN when x is zero/inf/NaN, otherwise one; condition is unordered equality to zero or abs(x) unordered-equal infinity.

Replace vector loop PHI used by same-index extracts and one cheap one-use binary recurrence with scalar PHI; extract each incoming lane, preserve operand order/flags, reuse duplicate predecessor values.
Replace variable extract from fixed pointer vector whose lanes share base and arithmetic-stride constant offsets with ptradd(base, index*stride + first offset).
Move extraction through cheap vector unary operation and copy flags to scalar unary operation.
Push extraction through vector binary operator by extracting both operands at the same lane and recreating scalar binop with copied flags.
Push extraction through vector icmp/fcmp and recreate scalar comparison with same predicate and copied flags.

Reorder a vector expression by applying the shuffle mask recursively to vector operands and rebuilding supported elementwise operations; remap constant insertelement index or drop its scalar when lane is omitted.
Rewrite C - ctpop(not X) as ctpop(X) + (C - bitwidth(X)).
Rewrite ctpop(not X) + C as (C + bitwidth(X)) - ctpop(X).
Rewrite disjoint-or(C, ctpop(not X)) as (C + bitwidth(X)) - ctpop(X).
Rewrite unsigned comparison against ctpop(not X) to comparison with ctpop(X) against bitwidth-C using swapped predicate.
For binop(select(cond,T,F), select(cond,cT,cF)) where cast selector is cond, build select(cond, binop(cT,T), binop(cF,F)) preserving operand order.
For binop(select(cond,T,F), select(!cond,cT,cF)) where cast selector is not cond, build select(cond, binop(cF,T), binop(cT,F)) preserving operand order.
Create new PHI from simplified/cloned edge results; when replacing identical users rewrite all other users to new PHI and erase them, then replace original operation.
Fold a GEP of a PHI when each incoming value is a compatible non-self GEP and the incoming GEPs differ at at most one non-struct index; clone common GEP and optionally insert a new index PHI.

Canonicalize each non-struct GEP index to the DataLayout index width: sign-extend narrow indices (or zext nneg when GEP has both nuw and nusw), truncate wide indices with compatible flags, and replace displacement through a zero-size element by a typed zero index.
Replace vector splat pointer/index operands with scalar operands, create scalar GEP, and resplat result to original vector element count when needed.
For one-use exact shift/udiv/sdiv index by constant, fold sizeof(T) into shift amount or divisor when divisible; reject signed quotient -1 to avoid INT_MIN/-1, then create exact op and i8 GEP.
Rewrite br (X && !Y),T,F as br (!X || Y),F,T; carry swapped branch weights from original condition when available.
Replace switch(X<<S) with switch(X), shifting case values down and masking X if shift can wrap.
Truncate switch condition and all case values when shared known leading zeros/ones permit a smaller legal integer width.

Push freeze through a one-use non-PHI operation that cannot create poison except by flags, dropping such flags and freezing its unique operand not proven nonpoison; if all operands nonpoison, remove freeze.

Move freeze from a recurrence PHI result to the sole start value, after traversing bounded backedge computation graph that cannot intrinsically create poison; drop poison-generating annotations and freeze start if needed.
